summary: CMU authors collect 38,709 grey-literature documents (7,630 web articles, 31,079 Reddit threads) about code review, filter with a Gemini 2.5 Flash relevance judge, LLM-code a stratified sample of 3,100 with Thematic-LM, and hand-build a causal theory of 26 constructs and 67 relationships (64 directed, 3 contested) on how coding agents reshape code review. A motivating mining study on the Agents in the Wild corpus shows agent PRs are merged faster and reviewed less, but that trend directions flip under defensible operationalizations.

claims.claim: Agent-authored PRs are reviewed less independently (40.1% examined only by the invoking developer vs 21.5% of human PRs) and the no-human-review share fell from >50% in mid-2025 toward the ~14% human baseline by early 2026
claims.evidence: §II-B and Fig. 1, details in Appendix 1; authors themselves show the direction of independent-review comparisons reverses depending on whether the invoking developer counts as a reviewer.

claims.claim: Review is the control point: AI does not fix the sign of its effect on software; the team does via reviewer expertise and process
claims.evidence: Theory in Fig. 2 with propositions P1-P17 grounded in practitioner quotes (e.g. G2048, G2935); explicitly not tested ('a proposed explanatory theory to be tested, not validated', §III-A1).

claims.claim: Effect of fully automated code review on quality/security is contested (P9); risk-tiered review policies lower latency while blanket gates raise it (P17)
claims.evidence: Quotes on both sides (G2836 vendor-sourced CodeRabbit 82% figure vs G1957, G1891); no measurement.

claims.claim: LLM-assisted grey-literature theory building is a scalable template (~US$0.35 per document)
claims.evidence: §III-A pipeline; relevance judge validated at Cohen's kappa=0.75 vs a stronger model (not humans); open coding by three LLM 'lens' coders; §VI concedes automated theory construction 'proved ineffective' and saturation point unknown.

patterns.note: Practitioner discourse splits on AI reviewers: throughput/latency gains vs missed deep defects and false alarms; P9 marked contested.
Human review framed as the control point; risk-tiered gating (only material changes) proposed as better calibrated than blanket gates (P17). Not tested.
Grey-literature and OSS-mining evidence, not a controlled field study.
Corpus includes spec-driven development threads (e.g. 'Spec-driven agentic coding is quietly making us worse at ... supervising agents'), but the theory does not model specs.

methodology.sample: 38,709 documents collected; 23,631 judged; 13,469 relevant; 3,100 coded (1,263 web, 1,837 Reddit); theory from ~2,700 sources / ~4,800 codes
methodology.baselines: n/a (theory building); motivating study compares agent vs human PRs
methodology.models: Gemini 2.5 Flash relevance judge; Thematic-LM multi-agent coders; LLM-assisted theme proposals
methodology.variance: Relevance judge kappa=0.75 vs stronger model; no human inter-coder reliability for open codes
methodology.ablations: Sensitivity of motivating-study trends to operationalization (reviewer definition)
methodology.contamination_controls: Acknowledges some sources may be LLM-generated; no detection applied
methodology.languages: n/a (discourse); subreddits include nine language ecosystems

standards.artifacts: Anonymized replication package with pipeline, 3,100 coded documents, quotes, theory model

biases.detail: Grey literature over-represents vocal early adopters and vendor advocacy (acknowledged §III-A1).
Relevance judge validated only against another LLM (kappa 0.75); LLM open coding not validated against human coders.
Quoted figures such as CodeRabbit's 82% planted-bug catch rate are practitioner/vendor claims, not verified.
All 67 relationships are proposed from discourse; none are tested; authors note a different team could draw them differently.

coi.funding: No acknowledgments section found in extracted text

verdict_reason: Transparent, well-scoped qualitative theory with a public pipeline and honest limitations; its propositions are hypotheses from practitioner opinion, not evidence, and its useful empirical nugget is that agent-PR review metrics flip sign under defensible operationalizations.
applicability: For a Java team where agents will author PRs across ≥4 ingestion repositories, the paper is a checklist of risks to design the review gate against: volume-driven review-depth collapse, polished-but-wrong code, missing design rationale (opacity) and comprehension debt. Spec-driven development is a plausible counter to opacity because the spec carries the intent the reviewer otherwise has to reconstruct, but the paper does not test that. Practical takeaways: tier human approval by risk (e.g. schema/contract changes to content delivered to front ends and healthcare-content correctness) rather than gating every PR; treat AI reviewers as assistive, not a replacement; and define 'independent review' carefully (the invoking developer is not independent) when measuring review across mixed agent hosts.

conflicts_with.detail: 'The End of Code Review' argues agents supersede human inspection; this theory holds human review is the control point and that full automation's quality effect is contested.
Agentic PR merge/reject mining; this paper shows such trend measures reverse direction under alternative operationalizations, cautioning against reading them causally.
